topic: Captain (YC W26) Review 2026: Automated RAG for Files

key_points: Captain is an API-first, self-tuning file search / fully-managed RAG retrieval platform from YC W26 (founders Lewis Lien Polansky & Edgar Babajanyan).
Indexes cloud storage (S3, R2, GCS, Supabase, Backblaze) and SaaS sources (Google Drive) into one queryable index.
Positioned behind one query API for AI agents; developer-managed, agent-agnostic (vs. end-user knowledge apps like Glean/Onyx).

Five layers shipped as one product: Search (sub-second deterministic API w/ filters/rerank), Iterate (MCP-triggered evals self-tune via captain_eval), Process (multimodal: scans, handwriting, tables, screenshots, audio, video), Engine (unified multi-provider vector+BM25), Sync (event-driven + scheduled sweep).
Demo 'Ask PG's Essays' (pg.runcaptain.com) set up in ~3 minutes.
Launch HN 'Captain (YC W26) – Automated RAG for Files' ~57 points on launch.

Founder positioning vs. DIY: 'the largest alternative is folks trying to build file search themselves — a lot to manage'; main similar product cited is Google Vertex File Search; distinguishes from OpenSearch (low-level engine), Glean/Onyx/Sana (end-user knowledge assistants), Kore.ai (agent orchestration).
Deterministic page-number citations for PDFs; exact bounding-box citations coming; links citations to source object storage.

Pricing transparency: $0.02 per credit; e.g. ~1,000 pages of new content/mo ≈ $295/mo for 15,000 credits + unlimited queries on startup-style plan (founders clarified advanced/basic processing tiers).

Skeptical HN feedback: 'you can already talk to files with Gemini / codegen entire pipelines', SaaS-only trust concern for sensitive docs, SOC2 'vibe auditing' critique, 'few months-years early' for optimization-focused buyers.
Captain v2 API stable (03 Jan 2026) with new docs site (docs.runcaptain.com) + interactive playground.
3x drop in search latency after migrating embeddings to object storage instead of a vector DB; claims better recall too.
Long-context document embedding (whole-file context + narrow chunk) plus automatic domain detection feeding BM25 to fix 'lost' domain-specific terms (drug names, non-English legal terms).
Precision optimized for healthcare, legal, financial use cases.
Partnership with HN team to build RAG forum search across 19+ years of posts; Python & TS SDKs.
Ragie hosted service shuts down 19 Jul 2026; many Ragie customers migrating to Captain — a direct competitive win / market consolidation signal.
Migration: connect original source (S3, GDrive, GCS, Dropbox) directly, no need to move data through Ragie first; most with access set up in <15 min.

Plans: Developer $0/mo (500 credits/mo, 1,000 queries/mo then $0.005/query); Startup $1,600/mo (83,000 credits/mo, $0.015 overage, unlimited queries); Enterprise custom (BYOC/on-prem, AWS PrivateLink, GCP Private Service Connect).
Credit pricing: Text $0.02/page (no OCR), Basic $0.02/page, Advanced $0.05/page (vision/layout for tables, charts, scans), Image $0.01, Audio $0.10/min, Video $0.40/min, Copy Collection $0.20.
Compliance claims: SOC 2 Type II, GDPR, HIPAA; secure handling, backups, 24/7 monitoring.

stats.fact: Captain is a Y Combinator W26 batch company; founded by Lewis Lien Polansky (CEO) and Edgar Babajanyan.
Captain v2 API cut search latency by 3x after moving embeddings from vector DB to object storage, and reports better recall vs. vector databases.
Developer plan starts free ($0/mo) with 500 indexing credits and 1,000 queries/mo; Startup is $1,600/mo for 83,000 credits + unlimited queries; usage credit unit ~$0.02/page.
Founders cited ~15,000 credits (~1,000 pages of new content/month) at roughly $295/mo for unlimited queries during the launch discussion.
Launch HN post for Captain reached ~57 points on Hacker News.
Captain demo 'Ask PG's Essays' (pg.runcaptain.com) was set up in about 3 minutes by the platform.
Ragie, a competing hosted RAG service, shut down on 19 July 2026, pushing customers to Captain.
Captain claims SOC 2 Type II, GDPR, and HIPAA compliance as of 2026.

angles: Automated/self-tuning vs. DIY RAG: Captain automates chunking, embedding, re-ranking, permissions and continuous re-indexing that teams otherwise hand-maintain.
'Spotty RAG' pain point: unreliable retrieval is the #1 complaint; Captain positions deterministic citations + self-tuning evals (captain_eval/MCP) as the cure.
Multimodal edge: indexes scans, handwriting, tables, screenshots, audio, video — beyond what plain text RAG handles.
Competitive shake-up: Ragie's July 2026 shutdown is a sign of consolidation in the hosted-RAG niche and a proof point for Captain's staying power.
The skeptic debate: vs. 'just use Gemini / vibe-code a pipeline' — Captain argues the maintenance + latency + precision matters at production scale.
Infra shift: embeddings stored as objects instead of a vector DB (3x latency cut) is an interesting take countering the 'vector DB is mandatory' orthodoxy.
Trust/SaaS concern: uploading sensitive company docs to a young startup — SOC2/vibe-audit skepticism as a buying objection.
